metadata.method: wandb.Api scan_history on val_kendall (logged once per epoch; peak_epoch == peak_index); drop = peak - final; peak_position_frac = peak_index/(n_val_points-1).
notes: comet-retrain-wmt sweep of 2026-08-17/18 (later found invalid): 36 completed runs with >=3 val points analysed; 2 runs of 2026-08-21 still running (n=0) and 1 aborted duplicate (kiwi-frac000agg, n=1) excluded from aggregates but listed.

comet-retrain: only the Bio-MQM sweep runs of 2026-08-14/15 (finished, >=3 val points) enter aggregates; failed/crashed kiwi runs of 2026-08-17 and utility runs (metadoceval, length_correlation, paragraph_data_prep) listed but excluded.

KEY MECHANISM: every completed run in both sweeps (and the July runs) has exactly 20 validation points after its peak - early stopping on val_kendall with patience=20 epochs. Run length is therefore endogenous (n_val_points = peak_epoch + 21), and 'drop_peak_to_final' is the decay accumulated over a fixed 20-epoch post-peak window, i.e. directly comparable across runs as a decay rate.

comet-retrain-wmt.characterisation: Yes, every curve rises then falls, but the bell is mostly shallow. All 36 sweep runs peak before the end and, because of early stopping with patience=20 epochs, then train exactly 20 more epochs while declining (mean drop over that fixed window: 0.015 Kendall). Severity is arm-dependent: ref-based runs (frozen or unfrozen) peak early (epochs 5-21) then drift down only ~0.008-0.012; kiwi unfrozen runs decline ~0.006; kiwi FROZEN runs are the clear worst arm with a pronounced bell (mean drop 0.035, up to 0.063 for frac000agg-frozen and 0.062 for frac000nat-frozen) - the head on the frozen encoder overfits steadily after its peak. Run length is endogenous (length = peak epoch + 21), and drop is uncorrelated with total length (r=-0.005): the arm, not the duration, determines the fall. Final-checkpoint scores understate every configuration and would distort arm rankings, most severely for kiwi-frozen; peak-checkpoint selection is required.

comet-retrain.characterisation: NOT flat - the Bio-MQM sweep of 2026-08-14/15 shows a much MORE pronounced bell than the WMT sweep: all 14 finished runs peak mid-run (epoch ~18-28 of ~39-49) at val_kendall ~0.367-0.372, then fall steeply over the 20-epoch patience window to 0.295-0.344 (mean drop 0.056, max 0.076, ~15% relative). Frozen and unfrozen arms are equally affected (mean drops 0.060 vs 0.052). The kiwi runs of 2026-08-17 in this project all failed after 1-11 val points (still rising when they died) and were rerun in comet-retrain-wmt.

overall_conclusion: Both sweeps exhibit rise-then-fall validation curves: training always overshoots the val_kendall optimum, and early stopping (patience=20 epochs) guarantees each run ends exactly 20 epochs past its peak, on the downslope. Bio-MQM (comet-retrain) is severely bell-shaped everywhere (drops 0.02-0.08 over the post-peak window); the WMT sweep is mildly bell-shaped for ref-based and kiwi-unfrozen arms (~0.006-0.017) but severe for kiwi-frozen arms (0.024-0.063). Post-peak decay rate is an arm property, not a run-length effect. Any evaluation using final/last checkpoints is confounded by differential post-peak decay - checkpoints must be selected at peak val_kendall (epoch 5-21 for WMT ref-based, ~13-75 for kiwi, ~18-28 for Bio-MQM).
